stops.note: from februa, purification rites held in mid-February, including the Lupercalia on the 15th; Julius Caesar's calendar of 45 BC gave it the leap day
Vulgar Latin had already dropped the first r (Febrarius); Middle English had forms like feverer
scholars restored the Latin -br- in spelling, though many speakers still say 'Feb-yoo-ary'; Old English called it Solmonað, which Bede (725) explains as the month of cakes offered to the gods

current_meaning: the second month of the year
